Add the corn, onion, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin, and black pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, until the onions begin to soften. Remove from the heat and add the shredded chicken and the blended salsa verde. Mix together to combine and set aside to cool slightly.
instructions.4: Roast the poblano peppers: While the chicken and corn mixture is cooling, arrange the poblano peppers on a baking sheet and broil them for about 5 minutes on each side until the skin is blackened and charred.
instructions.5: Cover the baking sheet with aluminum foil to trap the heat and allow the skin to soften for about 5 minutes.
instructions.6: Peel off the charred skin using a butter knife or your hands, getting as much off as you can. Make a vertical slit down the middle and scoop out the seeds. Slice the roasted poblanos into strips and set aside.
instructions.7: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
instructions.8: Prepare the tortillas: Heat the remaining 1/3 cup of olive oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Working one tortilla at a time, lightly fry each tortilla for about 10-15 seconds per side. Drain off any excess oil by giving it a little shake while holding it with tongs, then transfer it onto a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
instructions.9: Mix the cheese: In a large bowl, combine the shredded cheeses.
instructions.10: Assemble: In a 9x13 inch baking dish, add a layer of tortillas by placing 3 down the middle in a single layer without overlapping, and then 2 on each long end so half of it overlaps with the tortillas in the middle and half fold up along the edge of the baking dish. Spread ¼ cup of Mexican crema on top, then add ⅓ of the chicken and corn mixture, ⅓ of the roasted poblano strips, and ⅓ of the shredded cheese. Repeat this process with 2 additional layers.

w-mx-041.culturalNotes: Pastel Azteca is a traditional Mexican dish that combines layers of tortillas, fillings, and cheese, making it a rich and flavorful dish.

w-mx-042.title: Mexican Picadillo

instructions.1: Peel the carrots and potatoes.
instructions.2: Chop the potatoes and carrots into small pieces.
instructions.3: Preheat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
instructions.4: Add the ground beef to the frying pan and brown it (about 5 minutes).
instructions.5: Add the potatoes and carrots, stir and cook for 6 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the raisins and peas and stir.
instructions.7: Add the tomato sauce, salt, and black pepper and stir.
instructions.8: Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 20 minutes until the liquid has reduced and the potatoes and carrots have softened.
instructions.9: Taste and add salt if necessary.

w-mx-042.culturalNotes: Picadillo is a popular dish in Mexico, often served with rice or tortillas.

w-mx-043.title: Mexican Pozole Roja

instructions.1: In a large pot, add 2 cups of water and the drained hominy.
instructions.2: In a separate large pot, place the chicken pieces and add enough water to cover by a couple inches. Add the onion, cilantro, and 1 tablespoon of salt.
instructions.3: Bring to a boil then reduce heat to a simmer over medium low and cover. Cook for about 45 minutes until the chicken is cooked and tender. Remove the chicken pieces from the pot, strain and reserve the cooking liquid.
instructions.4: When the chicken is cool enough to handle, remove and discard the skin and bones and shred the meat.
instructions.5: Put the chicken and the reserved liquid into the pot with hominy. Place the pot over medium heat until warm. Add salt if needed.
instructions.6: For the red sauce: Place the chilies in a medium saucepan, add just enough water to cover and bring to a boil. Reduce to simmer and until the chilies are soft, about 10 minutes or so.
instructions.7: Put the chilies and 3/4 cup of the soaking liquid into a blender along with the onion, garlic, cloves, cumin, and salt. Blend until smooth.
instructions.8: Run this through a fine mesh sieve into a bowl, using a spoon to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard what does not go through.
instructions.9: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium high heat until it comes to a simmer, add in the chili liquid and bring to a boil then reduce to simmer, stirring occasionally. The sauce will thicken cook in total about 5 or 6 minutes and remove from heat.
instructions.10: Assuming your pozole is still warm turn up the temperature to medium high. Stir in the chili mixture and add salt to taste.
instructions.11: Serve the pozole hot with the accompaniments listed above. Make sure to squeeze lime over the soup, it makes the dish complete.

w-mx-043.culturalNotes: Pozole is a traditional Mexican dish served on special occasions and celebrations. It is known for its rich and spicy flavors.

w-mx-044.title: Rajas con Crema

instructions.1: Grill the poblanos over medium heat until charred all over, for about 20-30 minutes, turning the peppers every 10 minutes.
instructions.2: When done, place the peppers on a platter and cover with a bowl or plastic wrap for 5-10 minutes to steam the skins loose.
instructions.3: Peel the poblanos and discard the skins, then slice them into bite-sized strips.
instructions.4: Grate the cheese.
instructions.5: Cook the onion in a large pan until softened.
instructions.6: Add the poblanos, cheese, and crema mexicana to the onion.
instructions.7: You may also add corn as well as any salt or pepper, as desired. Heat through.

w-mx-044.culturalNotes: Rajas con Crema is a traditional Mexican dish served as an appetizer or part of a main meal.

w-mx-046.title: Chile Relleno

w-mx-046-i2.name: Monterey Jack cheese
w-mx-046-i2.standardAmount: 8 ounces (cut into long strips or shredded)

instructions.1: Roast the poblano peppers over medium heat until the skin is blackened. Place them in a sealed plastic bag for 10 minutes to cool.
instructions.2: Peel the peppers and cut off the stem. Gently open the peppers and remove the seeds and inner membrane.
instructions.3: Stuff the peppers with Monterey Jack cheese. Set the stuffed peppers aside.
instructions.4: In a bowl, beat the eggs with salt. In another bowl, place the flour.
instructions.5: Dip the stuffed peppers in the flour, then in the beaten eggs.
instructions.6: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Fry the peppers until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.7: Make the tomato sauce by blending the tomatoes, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, salt, and olive oil in a blender until smooth.
instructions.8: Serve the stuffed peppers with the tomato sauce on the side.

w-mx-046.culturalNotes: Chile relleno is a traditional Mexican dish often served on special occasions.

w-mx-048.title: Mexican Cinnamon Tea

instructions.1: Place the water and cinnamon in a medium-sized saucepan and bring to a boil.
instructions.2: Let it boil for 3-5 minutes, then remove from heat.
instructions.3: Let it steep for an additional 30 minutes or to taste based on desired strength.
instructions.4: Add honey to taste.
instructions.5: Serve warm.

w-mx-048.culturalNotes: Mexican cinnamon tea is a traditional drink that is very popular in Mexico, especially during holidays and special occasions.

w-mx-049.title: Fish Fillet with Garlic Sauce

w-mx-049-i4.name: Vegetable oil (or a mix of half olive oil and half vegetable oil)

instructions.1: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Set aside while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over low heat. Once hot, fry the garlic slices until they are golden. Make sure to remove them promptly once they are lightly golden; if you leave them longer, they will get a bitter taste.
instructions.3: If using the flour, dust the fillets with the flour lightly. Then, turn the heat to medium-high on the frying pan where you cooked the garlic. Once hot, add the fish and cook on both sides. The cooking time will depend on the fish’s thickness. It will be about 2-3 minutes per side for those fillets about 1/3 inch thick, and about 5-7 minutes for thicker fillets.
instructions.4: Remove the fish from the frying pan and place it on a cooling rack with paper towel underneath to absorb any excess fat.
instructions.5: Serve the fish garnished with the chopped parsley and golden garlic slices. (And if you add a little dab of butter, oh heavens!)

w-mx-049.culturalNotes: This dish is one of the popular dishes in Mexican cuisine, often served as a main course at family gatherings.

w-mx-050.title: Green Chile and Cheese Quesadilla

instructions.1: Preheat a comal for 1 minute over medium-low heat.
instructions.2: Warm tortillas for 1 minute on one side, flip and sprinkle some of the cheese on one of the tortillas, add chile, and top with another tortilla and press gently with a spatula.
instructions.3: Flip occasionally until quesadillas are golden brown on each side and cheese has melted.
instructions.4: Repeat with remaining tortillas and ingredients.
instructions.5: Top them with salsa and guacamole, if desired.

w-mx-050.culturalNotes: Quesadilla is a popular dish in Mexico, served as a snack or main meal.
